name: deep-research-profile
purpose: Defines when and how deep-research-agent should gather multi-step evidence and prepare detailed source-grounded reports.

reader_guide.summary: Use this profile when a task requires more than a short answer or implementation plan: broad retrieval, multiple research passes, evidence tables, contradiction handling, citation audit, and a long-form report.
how_to_read: Read trigger_situations to decide when deep-research-agent should be used.
Read depth_levels before choosing standard, deep, or exhaustive research.
Read deep_research_stages to understand the required pipeline.
Read report_contract before writing a final report.
Read citation_audit_rules before treating cited claims as ready to publish.
update_triggers: The user changes deep research expectations, report depth, or citation discipline.
A real search API, browser automation, file search, or MCP source connector is added.
Deep research reports repeatedly miss source quality, contradictions, or citation support.
The complete-deep-research input model or readiness thresholds change.

reference_links.title: Research Agent Profile
used_for: source ranking and citation grounding rules

reference_links.title: OpenAI API Deep Research
used_for: comprehensive source analysis and synthesis model

structure_rules.rule: Use deep-research-agent when a task needs a long-form source-grounded report, not merely a plan or short answer.
structure_rules.reason: The existing research-insight planner handles planning readiness; this profile handles report readiness.

structure_rules.rule: Deep research must record at least two research iterations so retrieval can adapt after early findings.
structure_rules.reason: Single-pass search misses contradictions, follow-up questions, and source gaps.

structure_rules.rule: A cited report is not ready until citation_audit_notes and unsupported_or_weak_claims are recorded.
structure_rules.reason: Citations can be attached to claims they do not fully support.

structure_rules.rule: Deep research must name report_targets before it is considered ready to write.
structure_rules.reason: Long-form work should leave a durable artifact path for review, history, and future reuse.

field_guide.meaning: When agents should route work to deep-research-agent.
Named depth options and minimum thresholds for channels, sources, iterations, evidence, and outline sections.
Mandatory pipeline stages for deep research report readiness.
Research lanes that help separate authority, context, quantitative support, community signals, and contrary evidence.
Rules for checking whether cited sources support report claims.
Output expectations for the final long-form report and its supporting artifacts.

trigger_situations: The user asks for deep research, a detailed report, a market/technology landscape, or a literature-style review.
The task requires many source types, conflicting evidence, or quantitative/source provenance before a decision.
The result should become a durable report under _research/ or a project docs folder.
The task may need multiple research lanes, such as official sources, papers, open-source examples, community signals, and contrary evidence.
citation_audit_rules: Every material claim should have a claim-to-source mapping.
Citations must support the exact claim, not only the general topic.
Partial support requires narrowing the claim or adding another source.
Unsupported or weak claims must be listed before writing or publishing the report.
Internal knowledge-base sources require knowledge-skeptic-agent validation before use.

preferred_formats: HTML report when visual scanning or navigation is valuable
